auditor.decisionRule: NO-GO if any P0 or P1 finding exists

checks.name: legacy-a-b-normalization-mechanical-uniqueness
checks.note: The null versus non-null mapping is mechanically unique, but M-06 fails because the mapping is normatively lossy.

checks.name: case-level-exact-core-consensus-prevents-fieldwise-hybrid
checks.note: The aggregation mechanics prohibit fieldwise and sectionwise composition; M-02 separately fails the authority for majority resolution.

findings.title: Resolver C cannot satisfy the protocol's own blindness requirement
evidence: Resolver preregistration section 3.2 says C must not even be told that primary admission was NO-GO because at least one A/B disagreement existed.
The same document section 0 states that exact fact, and resolver C's mandatory read-list includes that document.
Resolver C's mandatory read-list also includes resolver-protocol-seal-v1.json, whose knownPrimaryStateBoundary repeats admission=NO-GO and knownReason=at-least-one-field-disagreement.
findings.impact: Every compliant C necessarily receives forbidden outcome information before adjudication. The required blindness attestation is therefore impossible, and expectation bias cannot be ruled out.
findings.requiredDisposition: Keep C execution prohibited. A new immutable protocol/schema/seal version must give C a sealed, C-facing read set that does not disclose any primary outcome state.

findings.title: Legacy critical-mismatch normalization collapses normative distinctions
evidence: The original preregistration makes semantic, usage, and example mismatch values part of the exact normative fingerprint.
The legacy A/B schema stores each criticalMismatch as a free-text string or null.
Resolver preregistration section 4.2 discards all non-null string content and maps every value in a section to one generic *_CRITICAL_OTHER code.
findings.impact: Different substantive critical mismatches can normalize to the same controlled core and create false whole-case support; an equivalent mismatch that duplicates another categorical code can also normalize asymmetrically against C. Free-text exclusion therefore hides or distorts a normative distinction instead of merely removing rationale wording.
findings.requiredDisposition: Do not aggregate the current A/B forms under this equivalence rule. A new fail-closed design must preserve the original mismatch distinction or use adjudications collected under a pre-sealed controlled taxonomy.

findings.title: Case-level 2-of-3 majority is not authorized by the original preregistration
evidence: Original preregistration section 2 says an A/B field difference fails the entire admission and must not be resolved by majority voting or selecting one side.
Resolver preregistration section 5 adopts exactly one matching pair among A, B, and C as case-level 2-of-3 consensus.
The resolver also states that it does not retroactively modify the primary adjudication and may not relax the original v4 gate.
findings.impact: Although the rule correctly blocks fieldwise hybrid fingerprints, it changes the original agreement standard from exact A/B agreement to a majority-based salvage rule. The sealed contracts do not unambiguously grant that relaxation, so admission authority is not fail-closed.
findings.requiredDisposition: Keep resolver admission closed. Any future version must explicitly reconcile the base preregistration's majority-vote prohibition before sealing a resolver aggregation rule.

conclusion.reason: Three P1 findings exist; the predeclared decision rule therefore requires NO-GO.
conclusion.nextAllowedAction: Create and independently audit a new immutable resolver protocol/schema/seal version; do not create or execute the current v1 C form.
